result.title: Mitigating Video Hallucinations via Attention-Guided Representation Perturbation
result.summary: Video large language models (Video LLMs) often generate responses unsupported by the input video. Contrastive decoding (CD) can mitigate these hallucinations, but its effectiveness depends on how the negative branch weakens visual evidence. Existing methods rely on predefined perturbations or masking guided by question reconstruction, offering limited control over the model's visual reliance during answer generation. We introduce Attention-guided Representation Perturbation for Contrastive Decoding (ARP-CD), a training-free framework for constructing contrastive negatives directly in representation space. ARP-CD uses the attention mass assigned to visual tokens at the answer-prediction position to guide bounded gradient updates of the language model's input visual hidden states. These updates reduce visual attention and produce a negative input, whose predictions are contrasted with those of the original branch throughout generation. Experiments across four Video LLMs and four benchmarks show that ARP-CD outperforms representative training-free baselines in most model--benchmark settings, reducing hallucinations while improving general video understanding. Further analyses show that attention-guided perturbation directions improve negative quality and that the resulting negatives provide effective contrastive references for correcting the original predictions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的对比解码框架 ARP-CD：以答案预测位置对视觉 token 的注意力质量为引导，对输入视觉隐状态做有界梯度扰动以削弱视觉证据，构造负分支并与原分支对比生成，缓解视频 LLM 幻觉。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及视觉证据筛选与视觉旁路问题；其用注意力引导扰动、控制生成期视觉依赖的做法，可供核查 VLM 推理中视觉信息被使用或绕过的机制，以及注意力结构对视觉状态的影响。
